questions.title: Arithmetic Operations Drill
questions.description:
You are given two integers. Compute and print the results of all seven basic arithmetic operations on them, in a fixed order.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Seven lines, in this exact order:
1. a + b
2. a - b
3. a * b
4. a / b (true division, printed with exactly 2 decimal places)
5. a // b (floor division)
6. a % b (remainder)
7. a ** b (a raised to the power b)

Constraints:
1 <= a <= 20, 1 <= b <= 6
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(a + b)
print(a - b)
print(a * b)
print(f"{a / b:.2f}")
print(a // b)
print(a % b)
print(a ** b)

questions.title: Comparison Verdict Report
questions.description:
A validation script reports how two integers compare. Given a and b, print the boolean verdicts of four relational comparisons, each on its own line. Python prints booleans as True and False (capitalized).

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Four lines, in this exact order:
1. a < b
2. a > b
3. a == b
4. a != b

Constraints:
-100 <= a <= 100, -100 <= b <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(a < b)
print(a > b)
print(a == b)
print(a != b)

questions.title: Logical Gates Check
questions.description:
Four digital lines carry 0 (low) or 1 (high). Treat each value as a boolean (1 means True, 0 means False) and evaluate five logical expressions with and, or and not. Print each verdict as True or False.

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated values a b c d, each 0 or 1.

Output Format:
Five lines, in this exact order:
1. a and b
2. a or b
3. not a
4. (a and b) or (c and d)
5. not (a or b)

Constraints:
Each of a, b, c, d is 0 or 1.
questions.inputconstrains: each of a b c d is 0 or 1
questions.sourcecode:
a, b, c, d = [v == "1" for v in input().split()]
print(a and b)
print(a or b)
print(not a)
print((a and b) or (c and d))
print(not (a or b))

questions.title: Bitwise Toolkit Drill
questions.description:
Given two non-negative integers, apply the five core bitwise operators and print each result. Bitwise operators act on the binary representation of the numbers.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
Five lines, in this exact order:
1. x & y (bitwise AND)
2. x | y (bitwise OR)
3. x ^ y (bitwise XOR)
4. x << 2 (left shift by 2)
5. y >> 1 (right shift by 1)

Constraints:
0 <= x <= 200, 0 <= y <= 200
questions.sourcecode:
x, y = map(int, input().split())
print(x & y)
print(x | y)
print(x ^ y)
print(x << 2)
print(y >> 1)

questions.title: Augmented Assignment Trail
questions.description:
Start with a value v and walk it through four augmented assignments, one after another, in this exact order: v += a, then v *= b, then v //= d, then v -= c. Print the final value after all four steps. Note that //= is integer (floor) division applied at that point in the trail.

Input Format:
One line with five space-separated integers v a b c d.

Output Format:
One line with the final value of v.

Constraints:
0 <= v <= 1000, 0 <= a <= 100, 1 <= b <= 10, 0 <= c <= 100, 1 <= d <= 10 (the //= step always happens while v is still non-negative)
questions.sourcecode:
v, a, b, c, d = map(int, input().split())
v += a
v *= b
v //= d
v -= c
print(v)

questions.title: Membership Probe
questions.description:
A text-analysis mini tool checks how a word occurs inside a sentence. Given a sentence and a word, report three membership verdicts: whether the word appears anywhere as a substring, whether it fails to appear as a substring (not in), and whether it appears as one of the exact whitespace-separated tokens of the sentence. Python prints booleans as True and False.

Input Format:
Line 1: the sentence (may contain spaces).
Line 2: the word (a single token without spaces).

Output Format:
Three lines, in this exact order:
1. word in sentence (substring check)
2. word not in sentence
3. word in sentence.split() (exact token check)

Constraints:
1 <= length of sentence <= 100, 1 <= length of word <= 20, the word contains no spaces
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(sentence) <= 100, 1 <= len(word) <= 20, word has no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
s = input()
w = input()
print(w in s)
print(w not in s)
print(w in s.split())

questions.title: Parking Lot Fee Counter
questions.description:
A shopping-mall parking lot charges a flat rate of 30 for up to 2 hours (inclusive). Every additional hour beyond 2 hours costs 15 more. Given the number of whole hours a car was parked, compute the total fee with a single conditional (ternary) expression.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer hours.

Output Format:
One line with the total parking fee (an integer).

Constraints:
1 <= hours <= 24
questions.sourcecode:
h = int(input())
fee = 30 if h <= 2 else 30 + (h - 2) * 15
print(fee)

questions.title: Exam Qualification Verdict
questions.description:
A coaching institute screens students for a scholarship exam. A student qualifies only if every one of the three subject scores is at least 35 (no failed subject) AND the total of the three scores is at least 120. Print the verdict.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers m1 m2 m3 (the subject scores).

Output Format:
One line: exactly "Qualified" or "Not Qualified".

Constraints:
0 <= each mark <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
m1, m2, m3 = map(int, input().split())
total = m1 + m2 + m3
ok = m1 >= 35 and m2 >= 35 and m3 >= 35 and total >= 120
print("Qualified" if ok else "Not Qualified")

questions.title: Premium Discount Checker
questions.description:
A retail store gives premium customers a 15% discount, but only when their bill exceeds 1000. Everyone else (including premium customers with smaller bills) gets a flat 5% discount. The premium status AND the bill amount must both be checked together. Print the final amount payable after the discount, to exactly 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with the bill amount (integer) and the status, separated by a space. Status is "premium" or "regular".

Output Format:
One line with the payable amount, formatted with exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= bill <= 100000; status is premium or regular
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= bill <= 100000, status is premium or regular
questions.sourcecode:
a, s = input().split()
a = int(a)
rate = 15 if s == "premium" and a > 1000 else 5
print(f"{a * (100 - rate) / 100:.2f}")

questions.title: Shipping Cost Estimator
questions.description:
GreenDash Couriers computes a shipment cost with one fixed expression and no parentheses:

cost = 50 + 10 * weight - 15 * weight // 5

Python evaluates * and // (left to right) before + and -, so the subtracted term is (15 * weight) // 5, NOT 15 * (weight // 5). Reproduce the exact Python evaluation of this expression for a given weight and print the result.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer weight.

Output Format:
One line with the computed cost (an integer).

Constraints:
1 <= weight <= 40
questions.sourcecode:
w = int(input())
cost = 50 + 10 * w - 15 * w // 5
print(cost)

questions.title: Slab-Based Electricity Bill
questions.description:
A state electricity board bills energy in slabs: the first 100 units cost 3.50 per unit, the next 100 units (101-200) cost 5.00 per unit, and every unit beyond 200 costs 8.00 per unit. A fixed meter rent of 90 is added to every bill. Compute the total bill for a given consumption and print it with exactly 2 decimal places. Do not use min() or max(); compute the slabs with if / elif / else.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer units.

Output Format:
One line with the total bill, formatted with exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= units <= 5000

questions.title: Smart Home Feature Flags
questions.description:
A smart-home panel stores the on/off state of 8 devices in one byte: bit i of the mask (counting from 0, least significant first) is 1 when device i is ON. Given the mask and a device index, report the device state, then the mask after toggling that device (XOR with its bit), the mask after forcing the device ON (OR with its bit), and the mask after forcing it OFF (AND with the inverted bit).

Input Format:
Line 1: the mask m (0 to 255).
Line 2: the device index i (0 to 7).

Output Format:
Four lines, in this exact order:
1. "ON" if device i is currently on, otherwise "OFF"
2. the mask after toggling device i
3. the mask after forcing device i ON
4. the mask after forcing device i OFF

Constraints:
0 <= m <= 255, 0 <= i <= 7
questions.sourcecode:
m = int(input())
i = int(input())
print("ON" if (m >> i) & 1 else "OFF")
print(m ^ (1 << i))
print(m | (1 << i))
print(m & ~(1 << i))

questions.title: Food Delivery Fee and Coupon
questions.description:
A food-delivery app computes the final payable amount for an order.

Delivery fee: free for members whose order amount is at least 400 (membership AND amount must both hold). Otherwise the fee is 25 for distances up to 3 km, plus 6 per extra km beyond 3 km.

Discount: 10% of the order amount if the customer is a member OR the amount exceeds 900; otherwise no discount.

Print the final amount = amount - discount + fee, with exactly 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: amount and distance (km), space-separated integers.
Line 2: the customer status, "member" or "guest".

Output Format:
One line with the final payable amount, formatted with exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 5000, 1 <= distance <= 20, status is member or guest
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= amount <= 5000, 1 <= distance <= 20, status is member or guest
questions.sourcecode:
a, d = map(int, input().split())
status = input()
fee = 0 if status == "member" and a >= 400 else (25 if d <= 3 else 25 + (d - 3) * 6)
disc = a * 10 / 100 if status == "member" or a > 900 else 0
total = a - disc + fee
print(f"{total:.2f}")

questions.title: Blood Donation Eligibility
questions.description:
A blood bank screens donors against four criteria: age between 18 and 65 (both inclusive), weight at least 50 kg, haemoglobin at least 12, and at least 90 days since the last donation. A donor is eligible only when ALL four criteria hold. Otherwise print how many criteria failed. Do not use elif; build the verdict with logical operators and a ternary.

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated integers: age weight haemoglobin days_since_last_donation.

Output Format:
One line: exactly "Eligible" if all criteria pass, otherwise "Not Eligible - k failed" where k is the number of failed criteria.

Constraints:
17 <= age <= 80, 30 <= weight <= 150, 5 <= haemoglobin <= 20, 1 <= days <= 999

questions.title: Library Fine Ladder
questions.description:
A city library charges overdue fines in steps: the first 7 overdue days cost 2 per day, days 8 to 15 cost 4 per day (for those days only), and every day beyond 15 costs 6 per day (for those days only). Reference-section books pay double the computed fine. Do not use elif; express the ladder as chained conditional (ternary) expressions.

Input Format:
Line 1: overdue days d (integer).
Line 2: the book category, "general" or "reference".

Output Format:
One line with the fine (an integer).

Constraints:
1 <= d <= 60, category is general or reference
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= d <= 60, category is general or reference
questions.sourcecode:
d = int(input())
cat = input()
base = d * 2 if d <= 7 else 14 + (d - 7) * 4 if d <= 15 else 46 + (d - 15) * 6
fine = base * 2 if cat == "reference" else base
print(fine)

questions.title: Cab Surge Fare Estimator
questions.description:
A ride-hailing app computes a fare from three parts.

Base flag-down charge: 40.
Distance charge: 12 per km, multiplied by 1.5 when demand is "high" (surge pricing); multiplied by 1 when demand is "normal".
Waiting charge: 2 per waiting minute, but only when the waiting time is strictly more than 5 minutes; otherwise 0.

Total fare = 40 + 12 * km * surge + waiting_charge. Print it with exactly 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated tokens: km (integer), demand ("high" or "normal"), wait_minutes (integer).

Output Format:
One line with the total fare, formatted with exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= km <= 30, demand is high or normal, 0 <= wait <= 60
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= km <= 30, demand is high or normal, 0 <= wait <= 60
questions.sourcecode:
d, demand, w = input().split()
d = int(d)
w = int(w)
total = 40 + 12 * d * (1.5 if demand == "high" else 1) + (2 * w if w > 5 else 0)
print(f"{total:.2f}")

questions.title: Precedence Puzzle Solver
questions.description:
A maths worksheet generator evaluates the same four integers through three evaluation styles of one expression pattern, to teach operator precedence. Given a, b, c, d:

v1 = a + b * c ** 2 - d        (Python's real precedence: ** first, then *, then + and -)
v2 = ((a + b) * c) ** 2 - d    (strict left-to-right evaluation, ignoring precedence)
v3 = a + b * (c ** 2 - d)      (the c ** 2 - d part grouped first)

Print v1, v2 and v3, then the two differences v2 - v1 and v3 - v1. Do not use eval, max or min; compute each value explicitly with arithmetic operators.

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated integers a b c d.

Output Format:
Five lines, in this exact order: v1, v2, v3, v2 - v1, v3 - v1.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b, c, d <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
a, b, c, d = map(int, input().split())
v1 = a + b * c ** 2 - d
v2 = ((a + b) * c) ** 2 - d
v3 = a + b * (c ** 2 - d)
print(v1)
print(v2)
print(v3)
print(v2 - v1)
print(v3 - v1)

questions.title: Sensor Byte Checksum Builder
questions.description:
An IoT gateway validates a batch of sensor readings. Given n bytes (each 0-255), build:

checksum: the bitwise XOR of all n bytes (start from 0 and XOR them in order).
alarm bytes: how many bytes have bit 7 (value 128) set.
frame word: the 16-bit frame (checksum << 8) | alarm_count.
status: "ALARM" if at least one alarm byte was seen, otherwise "CLEAR".

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of bytes.
Line 2: n space-separated integers (each 0-255).

Output Format:
Four lines, in this exact order: checksum, alarm byte count, frame word, status.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, each byte is between 0 and 255
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, each byte is between 0 and 255
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    n = int(input())
    vals = list(map(int, input().split()))
    checksum = 0
    alarms = 0
    for b in vals:
        checksum ^= b
        if b & 128:
            alarms += 1
    frame = (checksum << 8) | alarms
    print(checksum)
    print(alarms)
    print(frame)
    print("ALARM" if alarms > 0 else "CLEAR")


main()

questions.title: Progressive Tax Engine
questions.description:
A tax authority computes yearly tax from income I (whole rupees) in slabs:

- up to 250000: no tax
- 250001 to 500000: 5% of the amount above 250000
- 500001 to 1000000: 12500 plus 10% of the amount above 500000
- above 1000000: 62500 plus 20% of the amount above 1000000

A surcharge of 10% of the tax applies only when the income is strictly greater than 1200000. Print the net payable amount (tax + surcharge) and the effective rate (net payable / income * 100), both with exactly 2 decimal places. Do not use elif; express every branch as chained conditional (ternary) expressions.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer income.

Output Format:
Two lines: net payable (2 decimals), then the effective rate (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= income <= 10000000
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    i = int(input())
    tax = (
        0
        if i <= 250000
        else (i - 250000) * 0.05
        if i <= 500000
        else 12500 + (i - 500000) * 0.10
        if i <= 1000000
        else 62500 + (i - 1000000) * 0.20
    )
    sur = tax * 0.10 if i > 1200000 else 0
    net = tax + sur
    rate = net / i * 100
    print(f"{net:.2f}")
    print(f"{rate:.2f}")


main()

questions.title: Logic Gate Verdict Panel
questions.description:
An industrial controller watches four safety sensors, each reporting 0 (triggered/false) or 1 (clear/true). From the sensor booleans a, b, c, d it evaluates three expressions exactly as Python does (not binds tighter than and, which binds tighter than or):

r1 = not a and b or not c and d        (read as ((not a) and b) or ((not c) and d))
r2 = not (a and b) or not (c and d)
r3 = (not a or b) and (not c or d)

Print r1, r2, r3, then how many of them are True, then "SAFE" if at least 2 are True else "INSPECT".

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated values a b c d, each 0 or 1.

Output Format:
Five lines: r1, r2, r3 (each True or False), the count of True results (0-3), then SAFE or INSPECT.

Constraints:
Each of a, b, c, d is 0 or 1.
questions.inputconstrains: each of a b c d is 0 or 1
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    a, b, c, d = [v == "1" for v in input().split()]
    r1 = (not a and b) or (not c and d)
    r2 = not (a and b) or not (c and d)
    r3 = (not a or b) and (not c or d)
    count = (1 if r1 else 0) + (1 if r2 else 0) + (1 if r3 else 0)
    print(r1)
    print(r2)
    print(r3)
    print(count)
    print("SAFE" if count >= 2 else "INSPECT")


main()
